purpose: Teach: 壷/林道/極楽/大昔/甘み/グリル/シェイクスピア/大黒

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが古い壷を大事にされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to treasure that old ceramic pot.
lines.style: Soft, distant voice opening on 'Gran.' Slow, deliberate pace. Each phrase settles before the next. A thread of affection running underneath the memory. Eyes unfocused, reaching back.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、林道で山菜を採りに行かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and your grandfather used to go out to the forest path to gather wild vegetables, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle correction wrapped in warmth. Slightly melodic rising on 'didn't he.' Not contradicting—redirecting with kindness. A small smile in the voice. Intimate and knowing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは極楽のような穏やかさを持っていらした
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father had a quietness about him—almost like paradise itself.
lines.style: Voice settles deeper into memory. Quiet wonder. Pause before 'paradise.' No rush. Speaking as though seeing it again for the first time in years. Tender and precise.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、大昔のお話を孫にされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — and you used to tell our grandchildren stories from long ago, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, slightly teasing lilt. A gentle pivot—she's reminding him gently of his own role. Playful underneath the tenderness. The tone of someone who's heard these stories many times and loves him for telling them.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが甘みのあるお酒を好まれた
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, your father had a taste for the sweeter sake.
lines.style: Quieter than before. A small, private memory—less grand than the others. Delivered as though confiding something intimate. Slight smile in the voice. Almost apologetic for the ordinariness of it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お庭でグリルでお肉を焼いて下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and you used to grill meat for us in the garden, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Bright and present. A shift—this memory is warmer, more recent in feeling. She's bringing him forward from the past. Affectionate, almost playful. The voice of someone who tastes the smoke again.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはシェイクスピアの劇を観に行かれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he'd go to see Shakespeare's plays.
lines.style: Voice lifts slightly—this memory has movement, culture, ambition in it. Still wistful but with an edge of admiration. Measured delivery, each word distinct. Pride underneath the distance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、家の大黒様のお飾りを大事になさったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and you always took such care of the Daikoku statue in our home, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Voice closes gently, intimately. A soft landing. The final word 'dear' carries the full weight of their life together. Not a question, a tender acknowledgment. Almost a whisper at the end.
